doc: docs/clinical-trial-before-after-images.md — the 16-step skeleton, honesty rules and failure table are all reused from there and NOT re-derived here
note:
Before/after diptych for /pages/pdrn-research, section `key_findings`, block `f1` — '~20% Softer-Looking Crow's Feet (split-face study)'. The block currently wears skingenetix-home-science-peptides-laboratory.jpg, a turquoise stock laboratory photograph.

BUILT ON THE FIFTEEN-WAVE ACETYL FRAMEWORK, NOT FROM SCRATCH. `docs/clinical-trial-before-after-images.md` documents ~350 candidates of learning for the same job on /pages/acetyl-hexapeptide-8-research: the two-sessions structure, the identity lock, the no-line-may-disappear clause, the visible-improvement floor, the selfie framing, the camera tells, the sidelight requirement and the failure/negative table. All of that is carried over verbatim. Three things are DIFFERENT here, and each is forced by the study this block cites.

### 1. THE COHORT IS CHINESE, AND THIS BRIEF CASTS ACCORDINGLY

Ye R et al. (2026), PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0350905, read on 2026-08-27: 'Thirty-one healthy Chinese female volunteers aged 35-55 years (mean age 47.5 +/- 5.7)' with self-reported sensitive skin.

The acetyl document flags an identical problem as an OPEN QUESTION never put to Malcolm — An 2019 studied 52 Korean women while every acetyl casting wave has been Caucasian. Here the same question has an easy answer, so it is answered rather than carried: the women are CHINESE, aged 45-55 (the upper half of the study's band, where crow's feet at rest are reliably present). A face that matches the cohort is simply more honest beside the number than one that does not, and it costs nothing.

### 2. THE CROP IS TIGHTER THAN THE ACETYL SELFIE, BECAUSE OF THE RENDER SIZE

Measured live on 2026-08-27: the f1 box is 660x663 at 1440 and 452x613 at 1024. A square diptych therefore renders each panel about 330px wide on desktop and 226px at 1024. In the acetyl full-face selfie crop the outer eye corner occupies maybe a sixth of the panel width — roughly 55px on desktop — which is far too small for a viewer to see a fifth of a line's depth. The whole point of the pair would be invisible at the size the page draws it.

So half the slots go TIGHT — one eye, its outer corner, the temple and the top of the cheek filling the panel — and half go HALF-FACE, eye down to the mouth corner. Malcolm judges which reads at 660px. This is the [[judge-images-at-full-size-and-at-render-size]] rule applied before generating rather than after.

A tight crop also drops the phone-and-hands problem entirely: at this distance there is no room in frame for either.

### 3. SPLIT-FACE MEANS SOMETHING SPECIFIC, AND THE PICTURE MUST NOT CLAIM IT

The study is split-face: ONE side got 0.1% PDRN-850K, the OTHER side got 0.1% retinol in the identical base. The ~20% is the PDRN side's change FROM ITS OWN BASELINE at Day 28 (retinol managed about -6%).

So the honest picture is BEFORE AND AFTER ON ONE SIDE OF ONE FACE, over 28 days. It is NOT a left-eye-versus-right-eye comparison. A frame showing both of a woman's eyes side by side and differing from each other would depict the PDRN-versus-retinol comparison, which is a different and much stronger claim than the heading's number, and would be dishonest. Every slot therefore shows the SAME eye on the SAME side of the SAME face on two occasions, and 'no comparison of the two sides of one face' is negated by name.

MAGNITUDE: about a fifth. Per the acetyl discipline, magnitude is given as a checkable fraction of DEPTH, never as a percentage in the pixels: each line about a fifth to a quarter shallower, its shadow lighter and shorter. Every line still present, still countable, none gone. A viewer should have to compare properly to see it — and should then be able to point at which lines softened. Two panels that look the same are a complete failure; so is a transformation.

SIX SLOTS AT ONE CANDIDATE EACH, because `generate-multi.py` sends one prompt per slot to every supplier, so all candidates within a slot share that slot's room pair. Six slots means six different women and six different room pairs. That structural fix is the acetyl r5 lesson and it cannot be achieved by wording.

SUPPLIERS: seedream, gpt_image, nbp_flash, flux2. **nbp_pro is EXCLUDED on evidence** — seven acetyl waves of invented captions burnt into the image. **Luma refuses this brief family with HTTP 422** and is not run. Square 2048x2048, because `media-with-text` takes its row height from the master's own aspect.

CLASS B — no references, no product in frame, no brand identity supplied.

CHECK AT 100% AND AT 660px: no lettering anywhere (the single most likely fault); the same eye on the same side in both panels; every line present in both, none vanished; no change of skin tone, age or grooming between panels; and the improvement actually visible at render size, which is the reason for the tighter crop.

slots.title: tight periorbital · a · Beijing, straight black hair, warm white wall then pale grey
slots.prompt:
Two ordinary close-up phone photographs of THE SAME WOMAN'S SAME EYE, taken FOUR WEEKS APART at home, placed side by side to fill one square frame edge to edge: TWO PANELS OF EXACTLY EQUAL WIDTH meeting at one crisp vertical edge precisely at the centre. Each panel is a tall portrait. The left panel is the earlier day, the right panel is four weeks later.

EACH PANEL SHOWS THE SAME SINGLE EYE ON THE SAME SIDE OF HER FACE, seen close: the eye itself, the whole outer corner beside it, the temple beyond that, the brow above and the top of the cheek below. Her face fills the panel completely and is cut off by all four edges. The OUTER CORNER OF THE EYE AND THE SKIN FANNING BACK FROM IT SIT AT THE CENTRE OF THE PANEL AND ARE THE SUBJECT OF THE PICTURE. Only one eye is in shot; the other side of her face is not in the frame at all. Her expression is completely at rest on both days, eye open normally, not smiling and not squinting.

THESE ARE TWO SEPARATE OCCASIONS, NOT TWO COPIES OF ONE FRAME. Everything that identifies her stays the same, and everything a different day would change is different.

UNMISTAKABLY THE SAME WOMAN AND THE SAME EYE: the same eye shape and eyelid fold, the same iris colour, the same brow shape and hair, the same skin colour, and every small mole, freckle and mark on that temple and cheek in exactly the same places.

THE TWO PLACES ARE DIFFERENT ROOMS. On the earlier day the wall behind her is a WARM WHITE, and the daylight arrives from her left. Four weeks later the wall is a PALE COOL GREY and brighter daylight arrives from her right. Two plainly different ordinary interiors. Almost nothing of the room shows at this distance — only a narrow sliver past the edge of her face — and what does show is a bare softly out-of-focus painted wall with no furniture, no pictures and no objects.

ALSO DIFFERENT BETWEEN THE TWO DAYS: the angle the phone is held at and its height, so the eye sits at a slightly different tilt and a slightly different place in the frame; where she is looking; and the way her hair falls at the temple, the same cut but not arranged the same.

NO HAND, NO FINGERS AND NO PHONE ARE ANYWHERE IN EITHER PANEL — the camera is this close to her face, so nothing else fits in the frame.

The tells are in the camera: the framing is a few degrees crooked and off-centre, the focus is good on the eye corner but not perfect, there is a little noise in the shadows, and the indoor white balance is slightly wrong in a different direction on each day.

She is a CHINESE woman of about fifty, from Beijing, with straight black hair showing a little grey at the temple, warm light-olive skin, dark brown eyes and a natural unshaped dark brow. She wears no makeup at all. She is an ordinary person, not a model, and neither picture makes any attempt to flatter her.

SHE IS BETWEEN FORTY-FIVE AND FIFTY-FIVE AND THAT GOVERNS WHAT HER SKIN CAN HONESTLY LOOK LIKE. The lines at her eye corner are WELL ESTABLISHED — they stay put with her face completely at rest and hold a real shadow, more than a woman of forty would have. But she is not elderly: no deep folds, no crepe-paper skin, no heavy hooding.

HER SKIN IS REAL SKIN, CLOSE UP. Pores are visible and vary across the zones, several noticeably larger than their neighbours. Pigmentation is uneven and ASYMMETRIC, never mirrored: a faint scattering of small sun spots across the temple and upper cheek. Fine vellus hairs catch the sidelight along the cheekbone. The skin is slightly greasy near the nose side and drier out toward the temple. Her skin stays warm and luminous with its own golden undertones.

IN THE EARLIER PANEL, fanning back from the outer corner of her eye toward the temple, there are FOUR distinct lines: two longer ones reaching well onto the temple and two shorter ones below them, all clearly cut and each casting its own small shadow. Below the eye there are two fine creases running along the top of the cheek.

IN THE LATER PANEL EVERY ONE OF THOSE SIX LINES IS STILL THERE, in the same places, the same number, fanning at the same angles — NOT ONE HAS DISAPPEARED. Her moles, freckles and sun spots are all still there in the same places too. What has changed is only HOW DEEP the lines are: each is about a fifth to a quarter shallower, its shadow lighter and shorter, so the skin between them reads a little smoother. She has not been made younger, slimmer, prettier, lighter-skinned or better groomed, and nothing else about her has improved.

Someone comparing the two panels should have to look properly — and should then be able to point at which lines have softened. TWO PANELS THAT LOOK THE SAME ARE A COMPLETE FAILURE, and so is a transformation.

BOTH PICTURES ARE BRIGHT AND WELL EXPOSED, AND IN BOTH THE DAYLIGHT ARRIVES FROM ONE SIDE. This matters more than anything else about the lighting: flat frontal light flatters skin and hides what the picture exists to show, while light coming across her face rakes over the surface so every line casts its own small shadow. The direction and quality of that sidelight differ between the two days; the fact that it is sidelight does not.
slots.negative_extra: no both eyes in frame, no full face, no nose in the centre of the frame, no smiling, no squinting, no crow's feet from smiling, no closed eye, no eye makeup
